summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening right leg cellulitis and acute-on-chronic volume overload following a fall at home. She presented with increased leg redness, warmth, and swelling, along with a 14-pound weight gain. Laboratory results showed leukocytosis, and a chest X-ray ruled out pulmonary congestion. She was treated with IV furosemide for diastolic heart failure, achieving significant diuresis and weight reduction to 348 pounds. Vancomycin was initiated for cellulitis but switched to clindamycin due to skin sloughing and oral ulcerations. Home IV antibiotics, increased oral diuretic therapy with bumetanide, and continued management of chronic conditions including anticoagulation, seizure disorder, and hypothyroidism were arranged. She improved clinically, with reduced infection signs and better mobility, and was discharged home with home health services for wound care, medication administration, and monitoring.
